Can you remind the BPO to send the bank statements?

Let me relay the main message, not word for word.

I lead a team of twelve at the BPO in Buenos Aires, and most of our instructions arrive second hand. The director speaks to the client, the client speaks to my contact, and my contact writes to me. By then, the message has often changed. Last month I received: they said the deadline is important. That is true, but it does not help me. What I need is the verb. Did they remind us, or did they warn us? Did they ask us to change something, or only suggest it? A good relay sounds like this: the director stressed that the pack must go out on Friday, and she asked you to send the bank statements by Wednesday. Now I know what is fixed, what is a request, and when. I do not need the call word for word. I need the main message and the right verb.

I am a controller, and I give feedback to three countries every month. I speak quickly in those calls, and I know that not everybody catches everything. So I always ask one person in each country to relay the main points to the team. The ones who do it well never write a transcript. They write three lines. The controller acknowledged that the March numbers were better. He urged us to close the open items before the fifth. He suggested reviewing the accruals with the BPO every week. That is all. When I read a relay like that, I know my message arrived. And if I see the word said five times, I know the team will have to call me again to ask what I actually wanted.
